thesis: The most dangerous spiritual state is not loud rebellion but the soul settling heavily into earth when Allah calls it to rise, because Allah can punish and replace the reluctant without His mission suffering.

flags.quote: Then the warning intensifies: if you do not march, Allah can punish, replace, and carry His religion on with other people entirely.
flags.issue: Mobilization-command passage; all four editions anchor 9:38-39 to TABUK (Tabari: 'وذلك غزوة رسول الله ﷺ تبوك'). File never mentions Tabuk, zero classical citations, no ikhtilaf, no tadabbur-vs-fatwa line while universalizing the nafir command. The inward generalization is the standard tadabbur move and benign — but done silently on a fighting-adjacent verse.

flags.quote: This is one of the Qur'an's most accurate descriptions of the spiritual lethargy that appears when obedience gets costly.
flags.issue: Unverifiable superlative, hedged by 'one of the' — rhetoric with factual cadence.

notes: Thesis directly carried (Tabari's iththaqaltum gloss; replacement threat explicit in all editions). Fix = 2-3 sentence Tabuk-context paragraph + tadabbur/fatwa note.

thesis: When fear of hostile people competes with fear of Allah, necessary struggle becomes a revelation of the heart, exposing whether fear is rightly ordered and where hidden loyalties (walijah) still live.

flags.quote: It is revealing that when confrontation becomes necessary in Allah's path, the outcome is not only strategic. It is also moral and emotional.
flags.issue: Fighting-command passage: no tadabbur-vs-fatwa line, no legitimate-authority conditions, and omits the ikhtilaf Ibn Kathir records (occasion: Badr vs Hudaybiyyah-breach; 'heal the chests': all believers vs Khuza'ah — Mujahid/Ikrimah/as-Suddi). Application is consistently inward and non-militant, which mitigates.

flags.quote: It asks about **khashyah**, fear textured by perceived weight, consequence, and significance.
flags.issue: Lexical over-claim: Tabari and Jalalayn both gloss atakhshawnahum as plain 'أتخافونهم'. The khashyah/khawf distinction is later lexicography presented as the verse's own insistence.

flags.quote: Five verbs opening five registers at once
flags.issue: Verb count and order verified correct, but the fifth verb (yudhhib) is in 9:15 not 9:14 — 'the verse' should be 'the passage'.

notes: All six tafsir attributions verified (incl. walijah = Tabari's 'البطانة من المشركين'). Strong file; repairable with one ikhtilaf paragraph + tadabbur/fatwa line.
